name: The Katzbach
summary: With Napoleon gone to Dresden, Macdonald advanced against Blücher's army in Silesia, crossing the Katzbach and the Wütende Neisse in a downpour. Charpentier's division and Sébastiani's cavalry climbed the narrow defiles onto the plateau beyond and found Sacken's and Yorck's corps waiting for them. Muskets would hardly fire; the Prussian and Russian infantry came on with butt and bayonet, and their cavalry rode down the French horse and drove the whole mass back over the edge into the swollen streams. South of the river Lauriston pushed Langeron back, but fell back himself when the centre broke, and in the pursuit of the next days, Puthod's division among it, Macdonald lost some 30,000 men.

forces.name: Brayer's Division
forces.summary: Souham's leading division, which came up the defile from Kroitsch onto the plateau late in the afternoon as the first French troops there were giving way, and was fed into the fight in the rain against Yorck's and Sacken's lines.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the Katzbach.
Its battalions were mostly young conscripts of the classes of 1813 and 1814. They are rated as ordinary Line, as they fought: the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit those who broke more readily.
Souham's old division, which he led at Lützen and Bautzen; Brayer commanded it under him here. Most of its regiments were provisional, two depot battalions of different regiments each.
Its two provisional light regiments, where the list allows one in a division, and the first brigade's four regiments, where it allows three, show as historical departures.
Regimental guns were lost in Russia and not replaced, so the division has none.
The division's two foot batteries, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Yorck's Corps
forces.summary: Blücher's centre. When the French came up onto the plateau Yorck's brigades went forward against them in the rain, the Landwehr with butt and bayonet as their muskets failed; Jürgass's cavalry charged with Sacken's, and the whole French mass was driven back over the edge into the flooded Katzbach and Wütende Neisse.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the Katzbach.
It rained all day: muskets would hardly fire, and much of the fighting on the plateau was done with bayonet, butt and sabre.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.

The grenadier battalions of Hiller's detachment are one regiment of four; the Landwehr regiments had four battalions each; Horn's brigade had four regiments and Steinmetz's no line regiment but the grenadiers. These, three or more attached hussar regiments where the list allows one, and line and Landwehr cavalry brigades together, show as historical departures.

The Brandenburg Hussars and 3rd Silesian Landwehr Cavalry were split between Horn and Hünerbein, each half shown as attached cavalry. The East Prussian National Cavalry, a volunteer regiment, is shown as Hussars.

Batteries beyond the one each brigade takes are in the corps artillery, as the list's reserve takes them; more than it allows, or a reserve horse battery with fewer brigades than the list wants for it, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.
